text: Segundo o refrán, a cada porco chégalle o seu…
gloss: According to the proverb, every pig gets its own... — San Martiño: «A cada porco chégalle o seu San Martiño» (11 November, the pig-slaughter season).

text: Que noite de festa enche Galicia de cacharelas, sardiñas e saltos sobre o lume para espantar o meigallo?
gloss: Which festive night fills Galicia with bonfires, sardines and jumping over the fire to scare off the evil eye? — San Xoán (23-24 June).

text: Se les a palabra «Roma» de dereita a esquerda, que palabra aparece?
gloss: Read «Roma» right to left: which word appears? — «amor» (love). The others are anagrams, not reversals.

text: Que río fai de fronteira entre Galicia e Portugal nos seus últimos quilómetros antes de chegar ao mar?
gloss: Which river forms the border between Galicia and Portugal in its last stretch before the sea? — The Miño. The Limia crosses into Portugal but is not the border.

text: Que gas expulsamos ao respirar e aproveitan as plantas para facer a fotosíntese?
gloss: Which gas do we breathe out and plants use for photosynthesis? — Carbon dioxide.

text: «Os pementos de Padrón, uns pican e outros…» Como remata o dito?
gloss: "Padrón peppers: some are hot and others..." How does the saying end? — "...not" («uns pican e outros non»).

text: En que estadio xoga os seus partidos na casa o Celta de Vigo?
gloss: Where does Celta de Vigo play its home games? — Balaídos. Riazor is Deportivo's, A Malata Racing de Ferrol's, Pasarón Pontevedra CF's.

text: Que personaxe de Cervantes arremete contra uns muíños de vento convencido de que son xigantes?
gloss: Which Cervantes character charges at windmills thinking they are giants? — Don Quixote.

text: Para o magosto hai 3 kg de castañas, e repártense a partes iguais entre seis amigos. Canto lle toca a cada un?
gloss: 3 kg of chestnuts for the magosto shared equally among six friends: how much each? — 500 g (3000 g / 6).

text: Cal destes animais NON pon ovos?
gloss: Which of these animals does NOT lay eggs? — The dolphin: a mammal, it gives birth to live young; it looks like a fish, which is the trap.

text: A Torre de Hércules, na Coruña, aínda funciona como faro. Que pobo a construíu?
gloss: The Tower of Hercules in A Coruña still works as a lighthouse. Who built it? — The Romans (1st-2nd c. AD). The Celts are the trap, via the legend of Breogán.

text: A maceira dá mazás, a figueira dá figos… e que dá a cerdeira?
gloss: The apple tree gives apples, the fig tree figs... what does the «cerdeira» give? — Cherries (cereixas): cerdeira is the cherry tree; the -eira pattern plus the cer- root leads there.

text: Que río pasa por Toledo e desemboca no Atlántico en Lisboa?
gloss: Which river flows past Toledo and reaches the Atlantic at Lisbon? — The Tagus (Texo).

text: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… Esta serie aparece nas espirais das piñas dos piñeiros. Que número vén despois?
gloss: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8... this series appears in the spirals of pine cones. What comes next? — 13: each number is the sum of the two before (Fibonacci).

text: Enches de auga ata arriba unha botella de vidro, péchala ben e métela no conxelador. Que é o máis probable que pase?
options: A auga mingua e queda un oco
O vidro afúndese cara a dentro
gloss: A glass bottle filled to the top with water, tightly closed, goes into the freezer. What most likely happens? — It breaks: water expands when it freezes.

text: En que data se celebra o Día Nacional de Galicia?
gloss: On which date is Galicia's National Day? — 25 July, the feast of St James. 17 May is Galician Literature Day, 24 June San Xoán.

text: Que tecla se preme xunto con Ctrl para desfacer o último cambio en case todos os programas?
gloss: Which key, pressed with Ctrl, undoes the last change in almost every program? — Z. X, C and V are cut, copy and paste.

text: Que bebida se queima na pota para facer unha queimada?
gloss: Which drink is set alight in the pot to make a queimada? — Augardente (Galician pomace brandy). Licor café is made from it, which is the trap.

text: Tes que pagar exactamente 5 € só con moedas de 2 € e de 50 céntimos. Cantas moedas necesitas como mínimo?
gloss: You must pay exactly 5 EUR using only 2 EUR and 50-cent coins. Minimum number of coins? — 4: 2 + 2 + 0.50 + 0.50. Three coins give 6, 4.50 or less, never 5.

text: Como chaman aínda hoxe en Arxentina e Uruguai a calquera español, sexa de onde sexa?
gloss: What do people in Argentina and Uruguay still call any Spaniard, wherever they come from? — «Gallegos», after the huge Galician emigration. Gachupín (Mexico) and chapetón (colonial Peru) are other names for Spaniards elsewhere.

text: Na gaita galega, como se chama o tubo con buratos no que o gaiteiro toca a melodía?
gloss: On the Galician bagpipe, what is the fingered pipe that plays the melody called? — The punteiro (chanter). Ronco and ronqueta are drones, the soprete is the blowpipe.

text: Setembro, outubro, novembro e decembro levan no nome os números sete, oito, nove e dez, aínda que hoxe son os meses 9 a 12. Con que mes comezaba, logo, aquel ano romano?
gloss: September to December carry the numbers seven to ten in their names but are months 9-12. So which month did that Roman year begin with? — March: count back seven from September.

text: Cal é o cumio máis alto de Galicia?
gloss: What is the highest peak in Galicia? — Pena Trevinca (2,127 m). Cabeza de Manzaneda (1,778 m) is the trap, being the best-known mountain resort.

text: Que escritor creou a Balbino, o protagonista de «Memorias dun neno labrego»?
gloss: Which writer created Balbino, the hero of "Memoirs of a Peasant Boy"? — Xosé Neira Vilas (1961).

text: Nunha fachada está gravada a data MDCCL. A que século corresponde?
gloss: A façade bears the date MDCCL. Which century is that? — 18th: M=1000, D=500, CC=200, L=50, so 1750; the 1700s are the 18th century (XVII is the autopilot trap).

text: Que deporte practicaba o cangués David Cal, ouro olímpico en Atenas 2004?
gloss: Which sport did David Cal from Cangas, Olympic champion at Athens 2004, compete in? — Canoeing (C-1 1000 m).

text: Os hórreos galegos érguense sobre pés rematados nunha pedra plana e saínte. Para que serve esa pedra?
options: Para que non suban os ratos
Para afastar a auga da choiva
Para secar o millo ao sol
gloss: Galician granaries stand on legs topped by a flat, overhanging stone. What is it for? — To stop rats climbing in (it is called the tornarratos); a rodent cannot climb round the overhang.

text: Cando en Santiago de Compostela son as 12:00, que hora é en Lisboa?
gloss: When it is 12:00 in Santiago, what time is it in Lisbon? — 11:00: Portugal is on Western European Time, one hour behind Spain all year (both change clocks together).

text: Que especia, a máis cara do mundo, se obtén dos estigmas dunha flor?
gloss: Which spice, the world's most expensive, comes from a flower's stigmas? — Saffron (Crocus sativus). Vanilla comes from orchid pods, cinnamon from bark.

text: O nome de que xoguete danés vén de «leg godt», ‘xoga ben’?
gloss: Which Danish toy's name comes from «leg godt», "play well"? — LEGO. Playmobil is German, Meccano British, Tente Spanish.

text: Cal das catro capitais de provincia galegas está máis ao sur?
gloss: Which of the four Galician provincial capitals lies furthest south? — Ourense (about 42.34° N), slightly south of Pontevedra (42.43° N); most assume coastal Pontevedra.

text: Cíes, Ons e Cortegada forman parte do Parque Nacional das Illas Atlánticas. Que outra illa o completa?
gloss: Cíes, Ons and Cortegada are in the Atlantic Islands National Park. Which other island completes it? — Sálvora. Arousa, Tambo and Toralla are Rías Baixas islands outside the park.

text: Na mitoloxía galega, que ser trae as treboadas e a sarabia que estragan as colleitas?
gloss: In Galician mythology, which being brings the storms and hail that ruin crops? — The nubeiro. The trasno is a household imp, the moura an enchanted maiden, the urco a spectral black dog.

text: A letra do himno galego é de Eduardo Pondal. Quen compuxo a música?
gloss: The words of the Galician anthem are by Eduardo Pondal. Who wrote the music? — Pascual Veiga. The others are Galician composers of the same era.

text: Que elemento químico ten como símbolo a letra W?
gloss: Which chemical element has the symbol W? — Tungsten (volframio), from its German name Wolfram. Vanadium is V.

text: Que arquitecto deseñou a Cidade da Cultura no monte Gaiás, en Santiago?
gloss: Which architect designed the City of Culture on Mount Gaiás in Santiago? — Peter Eisenman. Gehry, the Bilbao Guggenheim architect, is the trap.

text: Cantos corazóns ten un polbo?
gloss: How many hearts does an octopus have? — Three: one systemic heart and two branchial hearts for the gills.

text: Nun xogo de tenis o marcador está en 40-15. Se quen vai perdendo gaña os tres puntos seguintes, como queda?
gloss: A tennis game stands at 40-15. If the trailing player wins the next three points, where does it stand? — They have advantage: 40-30, 40-40 (deuce), then advantage; a game needs a two-point lead.

text: Franz Kafka naceu e viviu en Praga, daquela parte do Imperio austrohúngaro. En que lingua escribiu as súas obras?
gloss: Kafka was born and lived in Prague, then part of Austria-Hungary. In which language did he write? — German, the language of the empire's elite and of his schooling; Czech is the trap.

text: Se o Sol se apagase de súpeto, canto tardariamos en notalo na Terra?
gloss: If the Sun suddenly went out, how long before we noticed on Earth? — About 8 minutes: its last light (and gravity, at the same speed) takes about 8 min 20 s to arrive.

text: En que cidade tiñan a súa corte os reis suevos da Gallaecia?
gloss: In which city did the Suebian kings of Gallaecia hold their court? — Braga (Bracara Augusta), now in Portugal. Tui is the trap: the Visigothic king Witiza lived there.

text: Que partícula descubriu James Chadwick en 1932?
gloss: Which particle did James Chadwick discover in 1932? — The neutron. The positron was also found in 1932, but by Carl Anderson.

text: O primeiro Día das Letras Galegas celebrou o centenario da publicación de «Cantares gallegos». En que ano foi?
gloss: The first Galician Literature Day marked the centenary of Rosalía de Castro's "Cantares gallegos". In which year? — 1963: the book came out on 17 May 1863.

text: Fisterra debe o nome ao «fin da terra», pero o punto máis occidental da España peninsular é outro cabo galego. Cal?
gloss: Fisterra is named "end of the land", but the westernmost point of mainland Spain is another Galician cape. Which? — Cabo Touriñán (Muxía).

text: Que arquitecto deseñou a fachada barroca do Obradoiro da catedral de Santiago?
gloss: Who designed the Baroque Obradoiro façade of Santiago Cathedral? — Fernando de Casas Novoa (1738-1750). Domingo de Andrade built the Clock Tower; the others are Compostela Baroque architects too.

text: Que linguaxe de programación creou o neerlandés Guido van Rossum?
gloss: Which programming language did the Dutchman Guido van Rossum create? — Python. Java is James Gosling's, Ruby Yukihiro Matsumoto's, Perl Larry Wall's.

text: Na mitoloxía nórdica, como se chama a árbore xigante que une os nove mundos?
gloss: In Norse mythology, what is the giant tree that links the nine worlds? — Yggdrasil. Valhalla is Odin's hall, Bifröst the rainbow bridge, Asgard the gods' world.

text: Se a nota la vibra a 440 Hz, a cantos hercios vibra o la unha oitava máis aguda?
gloss: If A vibrates at 440 Hz, how many hertz is the A one octave higher? — 880: going up an octave doubles the frequency. 660 is the fifth, the common trap.

text: Que actor lle deu voz e movementos a Gollum nas películas de «O Señor dos Aneis»?
gloss: Which actor gave Gollum his voice and movements in the Lord of the Rings films? — Andy Serkis (motion capture). Elijah Wood played Frodo, Christopher Lee Saruman.

text: Cantos anos separan a primeira viaxe de Colón a América do regreso de Elcano tras completar a primeira volta ao mundo?
gloss: How many years separate Columbus's first voyage to America from Elcano's return after the first circumnavigation? — 30: 1492 to 1522.
